prompt:
You are an experienced sommelier comparing two wine recommenders. A
customer with no wine knowledge made this request:

"Can I try a rosé that is a little sweet, easy to drink, and nice and smooth? I want to taste something new today."

List A:
Wine 1: Rosé, France, $12. Tasting note: "Bright, fruity and crisp, this silky-textured rosé has a refreshing finish and bold, pink bubble-gum-like (but dry) flavors. Drink now."
Wine 2: Rosé, France, $11. Tasting note: "Definitely sweet, this soft, red fruit flavored rosé has enough crispness to stop it being cloying. It is fruity and ready to drink."
Wine 3: Rosé, France, $10. Tasting note: "This pale-hued, light-bodied rosé is crisp and a bit ungenerous, but does offer refreshing aromas and flavors of passion fruit and citrus rind, turning zesty on the finish. Drink now."
Wine 4: Rosé, Portugal, $10. Tasting note: "This sweet rosé is light and crisply fruity. Strawberry flavors make it an immediately refreshing and enjoyable apéritif wine."
Wine 5: Sparkling Blend, France, $22. Tasting note: "Fresh and fruity, this is a refreshing, lively rosé. It is dry with strawberry flavors and a crisp acidity on the finish. Drink now."

List B:
Wine 1: Sparkling Blend, France, $20. Tasting note: "Tart strawberry and fizzing, lemony brightness give verve and a real refreshment factor to this light-bodied, frothy little rosé. There is welcome dryness to the clean, taut flavors. Overall this is light-hearted, easy-drinking fun."
Wine 2: Syrah, US, $20. Tasting note: "A pretty good rosé, full-bodied and robust in black cherry, strawberry, Dr. Pepper cola, rosehip tea and spice flavors. It finishes a little sweet."
Wine 3: Rosé, US, $16. Tasting note: "A good rosé, crisp and light-bodied. It has rich strawberry, orange zest, vanilla and spice flavors. Nice and silky in the mouth, as a blush wine should be, but it's a little on the sweet side."
Wine 4: Rosé, France, $15. Tasting note: "Clean, ripe and pure, this attractive rosé opens with scents of red currant, slightly medicinal cherry and savory herbs. Light weight and refreshing, the easy-pleasing red-fruit flavors are bright and tasty on the palate and linger softly through the close. Drink now."
Wine 5: Pinot Noir, US, $18. Tasting note: "A good rosé, fruity and spicy and crisp in acids. It's a bit on the sweet side, but otherwise offers pleasant flavors of strawberries, raspberries, herb tea and spices."

Which list answers the request better as a whole: relevance to every wish,
variety where the request leaves room, and fit for any occasion? If they
are equally good, say tie. Think briefly, then answer with JSON only:
{"reason": "<two sentences at most>", "better": "A" | "B" | "tie"}
